question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom / Phrase.

To make merry
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"To make merry"** means to have fun and enjoy oneself. (आनंद लेना)

 
 
• **Example: **The villagers gathered** to make merry** at the annual festival.
 
 
 
• **"To enjoy oneself" **refers to having a good time and experiencing pleasure and happiness. (मज़ा करना)
 
 
• **Example: **We went to the beach **to enjoy ourselves **and relax.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'To make merry' **is **'To enjoy oneself'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To find loopholes **(कमियाँ ढूँढना): To search for gaps or weaknesses in a system or argument.

 
 
• **Example:** Lawyers often try **to find loopholes **in the law to benefit their clients.
 
 
 
• **To get married **(शादी करना): To enter into a marital relationship.
 
 
• **Example: **They decided** to get married after** dating for five years.
 
 
 
• **To make excuses** (बहाने बनाना): To give reasons that are not true or that try to hide the real reason for something.
 
 
• **Example:** He is always** making excuses** for being late to work.
